chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from a man, from Aban al-Azraq, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One of the most beloved deeds to Allah, the Exalted, is the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and the best of deeds in the sight of Allah is bringing joy to a believer, and the closest a servant is to Allah, the Exalted, is when he is prostrating and weeping.

key_terms.زِيَارَةُ: Ziyarah (visitation, specifically of graves or shrines)

ai.seo_question: What are the most beloved deeds to God according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Compiled by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith elevates the pilgrimage to Imam al-Husayn’s shrine to the status of a supreme act of devotion, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt as the locus of divine proximity. It uniquely links this physical act of ziyarah with the ethical imperative of bringing joy to a believer and the spiritual state of *baki* (weeping), illustrating the integration of ritual, ethics, and emotion in Shia piety.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. Abul ‘Abbās Al-Kūfi narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from someone, from Abān Al-Azraq, from someone who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

One of the deeds most loved by Allāh, the Exalted, is going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.), and the best deed in the eyes of Allāh is pleasing a believer. And the closest that a slave can be to Allāh, the Exalted, is when he is crying in the state of prostration.
